strings.name: LeBron James
strings.summary: James shaped the NBA through scoring, playmaking and longevity. He won championships with Miami, Cleveland and Los Angeles and became the league’s regular-season scoring leader. His public influence also includes education initiatives. He joined Philadelphia in 2026 after eight Lakers seasons.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones; competitions, affiliations and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive match log.
strings.influence.rationale: Historic NBA scoring and championship achievements combine with public advocacy and worldwide commercial and cultural influence.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Titles with three teams
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won four NBA championships across the Heat, Cavaliers and Lakers.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Scoring and public impact
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Set the regular-season career scoring record and supported education through his foundation.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: 76ers signing announced
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Philadelphia announced his arrival after eight seasons with the Lakers.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Third Olympic gold
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Won the Paris men’s basketball tournament with the United States.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Regular-season scoring leader
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s NBA career regular-season points record.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Lakers championship
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won his fourth NBA title and another Finals MVP award.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joined the Lakers
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Left Cleveland and moved his career to Los Angeles.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Cleveland’s first championship
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Led a comeback from 3–1 down against Golden State in the Finals.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First NBA championship
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won with Miami, then successfully defended the title the following year.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Moved to Miami
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Ended his first Cleveland spell and teamed with Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: First NBA draft pick
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Cleveland selected him first overall directly after high school.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Akron
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in Ohio and emerged at St. Vincent–St. Mary High School.
